description:
Markdown is the most complex existing component (~1000 LoC across
markdown.ex + markdown/{lexer, render, stream, inline}). Its
incremental-render shape — paragraph-boundary checkpoint, cached
committed iodata, theme/width as cache identity — is detailed in
the deck's §13 "Worked example: streaming Markdown."

Strategy:

  1. Keep `Markdown`, `Lexer`, `Stream`, `Render`, `Inline` as pure
     modules. They already are pure data + pure functions; nothing
     to move.

  2. Adjust `MdRender.committed`: today it is a single nested iolist
     tree. Switch to a list of {block_id, kind, iodata} tuples, one
     per committed block. ~30 lines of churn in render.ex; the
     separator handling moves to the consuming wrapper.

  3. Stable per-block keys via **monotonic block-id**, not hashing.
     Increment a counter inside %MdRender{} at append_segment time
     and attach the new id to the block. Hashing the source slice
     would cost roughly the same as re-rendering it — defeating
     the cache. Identity wins; the cost is giving up cross-message
     cache reuse, which is rare in practice.

  4. The TextBlock component (and ThinkingBlock, plus any future
     markdown-rendering entry) becomes a thin VDom wrapper:
       * use_state holds %MdRender{}.
       * On render, call MdRender.put(snapshot); store the new
         state via setter (called during render — see d06.2 for
         the "derived state from props" pattern).
       * Return a VFlow of [VMemo per committed block, VLines tail].
       * Each block VMemo's key is {:md_block, block_id, theme.id,
         width}; once committed, the key is stable forever, so
         block VMemos become permanent cache hits until reset.

  5. Width/theme changes reset MdRender (existing behaviour). Block
     ids restart from 0 inside the new MdRender; old cells from the
     prior generation go cold and get evicted via the standard
     hook-cell GC. Cost: one full pass over the source — same as
     today's MdRender.resize/2.

This relies on three framework features called out in d06.1:

  * VMemo thunks may return list/VFlow (block-level memoization).
  * Hook cells store arbitrary structs (the %MdRender{}).
  * Setters callable during render (the "derived state from props"
    pattern).

Acceptance:

  * Existing markdown rendering tests stay green (block-renderer
    fixtures: headings, lists, fenced code, tables, blockquotes).
  * Streaming smoke test in tmux: token-by-token append to a long
    response shows committed blocks settle into cache hits;
    telemetry confirms tail_lines bounded by current paragraph.
  * Performance smoke: a 100-block message at width 80 emits
    O(committed) cache hits and O(tail) cache misses per frame
    during streaming; full repaint on resize matches today's
    MdRender.resize timing within 10%. **No source hashing on the
    hot path.**
title: Convert Markdown subsystem (block-level VMemo + hook-cell MdRender)
